title: Assign Elements to Groups with Constraints
summary: Given an integer array representing group sizes and another array of elements, assign each element to a group based on divisibility rules.
statement: Given an integer array representing group sizes and another array of elements, assign each element to a group based on divisibility rules. For each group, find an element whose index is the smallest and divisible by the group size. If no such element exists, assign -1. Return an array indicating the assigned element index for each group, or -1 if no assignment is possible.
constraints: groups and elements contain positive integers; groups has up to 100,000 entries and values up to 100,000.
For each group value, choose an element that divides it.
Return the smallest qualifying element index for every group, or -1 when none divides it; elements may be reused.
hints: An element value qualifies for every group value among its multiples.
Visit elements by index and sieve their multiples, assigning only previously unassigned group values.
For each distinct useful element, walk value, 2*value, and so on through the maximum group; store its index only once.
Indices are processed ascending, so the first write to a group is exactly its smallest qualifying element index.
editorial: Indices are processed ascending, so the first write to a group is exactly its smallest qualifying element index.

tests.explanation: Element index zero divides groups eight and four, while index one is the first divisor of two; three has none.
The first threes divisor is index one, five uses index zero, and two and seven have none.
